answer: In this PoA design, an identity is accepted only after a prescribed chain of sequential modular squarings, each depending on the previous result; a Wesolowski proof lets peers verify completion efficiently. GPUs can run separate clone chains, but cannot shortcut an individual chain through parallelism, so each clone incurs its own physical delay and hardware cost—a ledge against cheap Sybil scaling, not a ban on parallel hardware. The pigment of a claim is tested over that voyage.
